chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Advice to young musicians: study the heritage
summary: Collins urges young players to listen to earlier recordings, since what they do extends what was done before.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Now, I -- it's just -- one thing I want to say is for the young musician we have some fine young musicians now, on all instruments. That's piano, drums, guitar, trumpet, whatever. But for them I think they should realize that what they are doing now is essentially an extension of what has been done before. And they should all go back just dig and listen to what was done before, and see how great the musicians of these different eras were and what they really contributed. You know. Because these musicians now -- I'm sure a lot of them think that they are creating and, you know, what they are doing has not been done before, and they forget. But if they will listen to some of the recordings of some of the things that were done before, they would see that it has been done before.
